judgements.justification: B's raises came from Reviewer_RJD5, the most exact reviewer on either side, and Reviewer_yRN6 at confidence 4; the self-declared non-expert Reviewer_yRQF did not raise.
The committees read the paper as different kinds of contribution (A a performance method, B an insight), which is R16, not one type held to two bars.
Reviewer_yRQF's 8 rests partly on the claim that r2v 'works empirically the best', which Fig. 3 contradicts on Airport, AstroPh and most of HepTh.
No A reviewer answered the rebuttal, so none acknowledged a resolved concern while keeping the score.
A's meta-review still cites 'lacking comparison' after the rebuttal added Fairwalk, GAT and related-work text, while B raised scores 'based on your edits'.
Every stated change of position in B came with a score edit, and no A reviewer stated a changed position.
No extra reviewer appears in either committee.
Clarity was not the deciding axis, and the non-expert Reviewer_yRQF praised the clarity rather than penalising it.
Both B raises came with stated reasons in comments; no reviewer raised silently.
Neither chair discounted a low rating for non-engagement; A counted its silent reviewers and B had no detractor.
B's only rating above 7 is Reviewer_yRQF's five-sentence praise review, not a detailed, checked reading.
No reviewer in either committee admitted reading only part of the paper.
A judged the paper against prior debiasing methods, not from a theoretical tradition that contested its premise.
B's meta-review argues only that concerns were clarified and gives no reason for the spotlight tier.

A's reviewers knew the degree-debiasing literature (APPR, Lasagne, Fairwalk, role2vec) and checked novelty against it; B never raised it, scrutinised derivations and setup, and Reviewer_yRQF left originality to others.

A's meta-review says 'lacking comparison' and that discussion 'converged on rejection' without mentioning the rebuttal's Fairwalk and GAT baselines or Reviewer_MjL3's 6, and no discussion is on the record.
Neither committee raised a narrow-audience or wrong-venue concern.
B had no low-scoring detractor, and A rejected rather than argued for acceptance.
Both committees received new baselines on the same day (Fairwalk and GAT in A; offset-only and NetMF in B), so A did not get only promised text.
A's highest-confidence review (Reviewer_HWNH, 5) rated low, and in B the higher-confidence reviewers did not rate above the low-confidence ones.
No reviewer added an objection after the response period closed.
The rating gap follows different issues raised and rebuttal raises in B, not leniency for equally favourable text.
No reviewer or chair judged the headline claim or title overstated; A's objection was inconsistent gains and missing prior work.
B's reviewers committed to 6, 6, 8, 7 and B gave a spotlight; no committee's flat marginal scores capped a tier.
